items.title: vercel's agent-desktop takes today's biggest star gain at 3,792
items.summary:
agent-desktop gives agents a cli over desktop apps by reading each app's accessibility tree instead of guessing from screenshots.
it added 3,792 stars today to reach 11,997, more than any other repo on github trending, and was pushed again this afternoon.

items.title: claude-mem holds the top trending slot with 1,138 stars
items.summary:
claude-mem captures what an agent does in a session, compresses it with a model and injects the useful parts into later sessions.
it added 1,138 stars today to reach 111,510 and sits first on github trending, ahead of agent-desktop on raw stars but behind it on velocity.

items.title: mattpocock's agent skills repo enters with 1,164 stars
items.summary:
the repo is a plain directory of skills for coding agents, taken straight from the author's own dot-agents folder.
it added 1,164 stars today and now sits on 311,055 total, with its last push on 1 november.

items.title: scrapling adds 1,658 stars for scraping everything from one request to a crawl
items.summary:
scrapling is a python scraping framework that handles a single fetch, stealth browser sessions and full crawls behind one api.
it added 1,658 stars today to reach 94,053 and was last pushed on monday evening.

items.title: colibri adds 803 stars for running huge mixture-of-experts models on one box
items.summary:
colibri keeps hot experts on the gpu, warm ones in ram and cold ones on nvme, so a frontier moe model can run on hardware you own.
it added 803 stars today to reach 47,045, is written in c and was pushed this afternoon.

items.title: heretic adds 699 stars for editing model behaviour without retraining
items.summary:
heretic is a training-free tool that edits a language model's weights to remove refusals, cut slop and reduce sycophancy.
it added 699 stars today to reach 38,572, with a fresh push this afternoon and an agpl licence.

items.title: worktrunk adds 437 stars for git worktrees aimed at parallel agents
items.summary:
worktrunk is a rust cli that makes git worktrees easy to create, list and clean up when several agents work in parallel.
it added 437 stars today to reach 10,333 and was pushed again at 15:43 utc.

items.title: claude-code-game-studios adds 1,181 stars for a 49-agent studio
items.summary:
the repo turns claude code into a game studio with 49 agents, 72 workflow skills and a studio-style coordination system.
it added 1,181 stars today to reach 34,361, with no code push since 19 october.

items.title: us confirms 'defensive' strikes on iran's qeshm island
items.summary:
us officials told cbs and the bbc that the strikes were limited and defensive, answering irgc fire at a us aircraft over the strait.
the irgc says it shot down two mq-170 drones south of qeshm and an mq-9 east of hormuz, and trump says the target was an anti-aircraft site hit the night it was finished.
items.change: the us account hardened: officials now say the strike answered irgc fire on a us aircraft, while iran says it downed three drones and trump called the target an anti-aircraft site.

items.title: trump says the us stops paying israel $4bn a year at the end of december
items.summary:
trump told fox news that he and netanyahu agreed months ago to end the $4bn annual payment by the end of this year, and that israel can still buy us weapons.
the white house gave no detail on which funds are meant, and netanyahu's office has not confirmed it, while the current $38bn memorandum runs to 2028.
items.change: new: a sitting us president said on the record that direct aid to israel ends in december, a claim israel has not confirmed.

items.title: trump says there is 'no rush' on iran as voters go to the polls
items.summary:
trump told axios he is in no rush to widen the war because the us has 'crippled them financially', and told fox he could still hit pickaxe mountain in 'one hour'.
us officials separately told the wall street journal that washington has run 'limited strikes' for weeks, kept quiet to avoid signalling a bigger campaign.
items.change: the midterms are under way with no new strike ordered, but us officials now admit to a quiet run of limited strikes rather than a one-off.

items.title: qatar says washington and tehran are studying its proposals
items.summary:
qatar's spokesman said a delegation spent more than three hours in tehran on monday and both sides are now reviewing doha's proposal, with mediators trading drafts in real time.
iran's armed forces chief set five conditions, including an end to hostilities on all fronts, full sanctions relief, reparations and recognition of iranian sovereignty over hormuz.
items.change: qatar went public with the shuttle: a delegation was in tehran for more than three hours and both capitals are reviewing the same text, while iran's military named its price.

items.title: israel's opposition backs eisenkot, but shas stays with netanyahu
items.summary:
the five opposition leaders met in herzliya and agreed to recommend gadi eisenkot to president herzog, with negotiating teams starting on coalition terms immediately.
shas then said it would recommend netanyahu, leaving the blocs at 53-48-19 before herzog opens consultations on wednesday and thursday.
items.change: the opposition formalised its pick of eisenkot and opened talks, but shas answered by backing netanyahu, so neither bloc has 61 seats.

items.title: saudi coalition intercepts a drone over mecca as taiz hospitals run short
items.summary:
the coalition's spokesman said it destroyed a drone over the makkah region, a day after it reported downing a ballistic missile and two drones fired from yemen.
unfpa says only five of taiz's 27 emergency maternal hospitals are partly working, with 13,000 pregnant women short of care and about 300,000 displaced since august.
items.change: the coalition reported another interception over makkah, this time a drone, while the un put numbers on the collapse of maternal care in taiz.

items.title: syria says it foiled a hezbollah-linked plot on the homs refinery
items.summary:
syria's general intelligence service said it arrested two men and seized explosives prepared to hit the homs oil refinery in a pre-emptive operation with internal security.
hezbollah denied the charge and said it has no presence in syria, as damascus presses a wider case against the group after assad's fall.
items.change: new: damascus announced a pre-emptive arrest over a refinery bombing plot and pointed at hezbollah, which denied it.

items.title: qatar calls hormuz navigation non-negotiable after the al-mayda hit
items.summary:
qatar's spokesman said freedom of navigation in the strait is non-negotiable and that any new attack, on iranian soil or on shipping, would hit the talks.
he restated qatar's condemnation of the attack on its lng carrier al-mayda, and crude fell for a second session as traders priced in the diplomacy.
items.change: qatar turned the al-mayda attack into a public red line on hormuz navigation, and crude kept falling despite the risk.

items.title: tech steadies and the s&p 500 gains 0.5% as america votes
items.summary:
the s&p 500 rose 0.5% to 7,576 and the nasdaq-100 gained 0.8% to 28,214, a day after the index closed more than 10% below its october record.
the dow slipped 0.3%, the vix fell 3.8% to 20.3 and the 10-year yield rose to 4.94% as investors waited for the midterm results.

items.title: brent falls a second day to about $103 on hopes of an iran deal
items.summary:
brent fell 1.6% to $103.14 and wti dropped 0.8% to $95.72, extending monday's 7% slide as traders bet on a diplomatic end to the war.
crude had jumped after the qeshm strike, then gave it back when qatar said washington and tehran were reviewing the same proposals.

items.title: apple falls 2.7% after its holiday margin guide misses
items.summary:
apple guided december-quarter gross margin to 45-46%, below the 46.3% analysts expected, and the stock fell 2.7% to $329.
cfo kevan parekh blamed higher memory costs and the siri ai ramp, which would make a third straight quarterly margin decline.

items.title: shopify drops 7% and palantir 3.7% while ferrari and yum beat
items.summary:
shopify fell 7% after missing on gross merchandise volume and subscription profit, and palantir dropped 3.7% as analysts flagged slower contract-value growth.
ferrari rose 2.5% on a guidance raise, yum added 0.8% despite a cyclospora hit at taco bell, and disney slipped as it planned several thousand layoffs.

items.title: jolts beats at 7.52m openings and factory orders jump 1.8%
items.summary:
september job openings rose 333,000 to 7.52m, well above the 7.1m forecast, while quits hit their highest since march 2025 and layoffs fell.
factory orders rose 1.8% against 1.2% expected, and the next tests are wednesday's adp and ism services before friday's payrolls, seen at 59,000.

items.title: amd and amgen lead tonight's earnings queue after a mixed morning
items.summary:
amd reports after the close with a $1.68 consensus, joined by amgen, arista, booking and block.
the morning slate was split: pfizer raised its outlook, ferrari lifted guidance and yum beat, while shopify missed and apple's margin warning set the tone.

items.title: a democratic sweep is the midterm result most likely to jolt stocks
items.summary:
control of congress is being decided today, and cnbc reports that a democratic sweep is the result most likely to move equities sharply.
bill ackman warned the market has become a 'casino' as speculative trading grows, with the vix still above 20 going into the vote.

items.title: liverpool take a perfect european record to kuyt's fenerbahce
items.summary:
liverpool have won all three champions league games and sit third in the league phase before facing a fenerbahce side now run by interim boss dirk kuyt.
kick-off is 20:45 riyadh at sukru saracoglu, and the hosts lost 2-1 at home to goztepe on saturday and were beaten 6-0 at aston villa in europe.

items.title: gravenberch misses istanbul with a heel injury
items.summary:
ryan gravenberch did not travel to turkey after a heel problem ruled him out, and he stayed at the axa training centre for treatment.
the echo counts seven absentees for istanbul, with frimpong, bradley, leoni and ekitike already out.

items.title: szoboszlai and munoz travel as liverpool name a 22-man squad
items.summary:
szoboszlai and munoz are in the squad after coming through their comebacks at arsenal, alongside ngumoha, danns, mcconnell, koumas and chambers.
alisson, van dijk, wirtz, isak and gakpo also travel, while gravenberch, frimpong, bradley, leoni and ekitike stay behind.

items.title: kuyt says facing liverpool is 'a very, very special occasion'
items.summary:
dirk kuyt, who made 285 appearances for liverpool and won the league with fenerbahce as a player, took interim charge last week after ismail kartal resigned.
he said the tie means a lot to him but 'i'm not the important person, it's the club', and called fenerbahce's first european campaign in 18 years a special achievement.

items.title: ngumoha makes the istanbul squad with gravenberch out
items.summary:
rio ngumoha is in the 22-man travelling party after the echo reported he was on standby for istanbul.
iraola has rotated heavily through a run of nine games in 29 days and made seven changes for the arsenal defeat.

items.title: real madrid are watching munoz, with mac allister's deal unresolved
items.summary:
a spanish report relayed by the echo says real madrid are tracking victor munoz, who came through their academy and has no buy-back clause at liverpool.
the echo frames it against alexis mac allister entering the final 12 months of his deal, so treat it as monitoring rather than a bid.

meta.reliability: medium - spanish report (AS) relayed by the echo

items.title: arsenal's first league win at anfield since 2012 leaves liverpool fifth
items.summary:
kai havertz scored after alisson's pass went wrong and arsenal won 1-0 at anfield for the first time in the premier league since 2012.
liverpool are fifth and nine points off the top after a first league defeat in six, with no shot on target at home.

items.title: hackett says timber should have been sent off for the pull on isak
items.summary:
former referee keith hackett said jurrien timber should have been sent off as well as conceding the penalty for his shirt pull on alexander isak.
the echo reports his view that var should have sent andy madley to the monitor, and iraola said the isak incident was a clear penalty.
